- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 10–15 days of 30d window).
- Forecasts tend to peak too early or too high after recent spikes, then sharply drop — suggesting overshoot and failure to capture mean reversion.
- Model underestimates prices in the latter half of the 30d window, particularly after mid-term peaks.
- Forecast bias is stronger in periods with high volatility or sharp downward moves — model fails to adjust downward quickly enough.
- Model exhibits lag in responding to recent price drops — often takes 2–3 days to correct downward trend.
- In cases of sustained upward trends, model overreacts to short-term volatility and fails to smooth out the trend.
- Forecasts show persistent bias toward higher values when historical mean is low — model “clings” to recent highs even when context suggests mean reversion.
- Model underestimates downward momentum in the final 5–10 days of the forecast window — often misses the final correction or “bottoming” phase.
